items.name: TypeSafe AI — Jev (System One Models)
items.summary: TypeSafe AI broke two years of stealth on Sep 15 with Jev, the first "System One" model — a decision engine that returns typed, calibrated outputs instead of chat text, aimed at 100x-faster structured automation decisions at $0.042/M input tokens. Founded by ex-OpenAI RLHF/InstructGPT co-author Diogo Almeida, the launch came with a $40M DCVC-led seed round.

items.name: OpenAI — Astra for Law
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Astra for Law on Sep 17: GPT-6 Astra configured with a dedicated 230M+ URL legal search index and firm-level controls, offered to selected law firms via Trusted Access (26 legal plugins included). OpenAI reports 54% correctness on Vals AI's Legal Research Bench vs 38.7% for base GPT-6 Astra with web search.

items.name: Salesforce — Koa (CRM reasoning model)
items.summary: Salesforce and NVIDIA announced Koa on Sep 15, Salesforce's first CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on synthetic data drawn from 27 years of Salesforce CRM deployments. Salesforce claims it matches or exceeds leading models on its CRM Bench with 3x fewer errors; pilots start in October.

items.name: PrismML — Bonsai 2 27B
items.summary: Caltech spinout PrismML released Bonsai 2 27B (Sep 17), compressing Alibaba's open Qwen3.8 27B into a 5.9 GB reasoning model — a 9–10x memory cut small enough to run on a PC and possibly a high-end smartphone. It bets that capable reasoning models don't need to be large, with a rumored Apple partnership declined comment by CEO Babak Hassibi.

items.name: Aikido — Altar (open-weight cybersecurity model)
items.summary: Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido released Altar on Sep 21, an open-weight AI model for cybersecurity tasks — a compressed, customized version of Z.AI's GLM-5.3 designed to run locally so companies can use defensive AI tools without sending sensitive code to external providers. The company, valued at ~$1B in January, is deploying it for customers like Belfius bank.
